# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 1

**1** The vision which I saw, brothers and sisters, was this: **2** After I had fasted many days and asked God to show me the revelation which he had promised me through the aged woman — that same night the aged woman appeared to me and said, "Since you hunger so much for knowledge and are so zealous in seeking it, come early in the morning to the field where you farm, and at the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what it is necessary for you to see." **3** I asked her, saying, "Lady, in what part of the field?" And she said, "Wherever you wish." I chose a good and quiet place. But before I could speak and give her the location, she said, "I will come wherever you wish." **4** So I went, brothers and sisters, to the field and counted the hours, and came to the place where I had appointed her to come, and I saw a couch of ivory placed there, and on the couch lay a linen cushion and over it a spread of fine linen. **5** When I saw these things lying there and no one in the place, I was seized with wonder and a kind of trembling came over me and my hair stood on end. And as I was astonished, for I was alone, I recovered myself. When I regained composure, I saw the aged woman approaching with a little book in her hand, and she sat down alone and greeted me: "Greetings, Hermas." **6** In grief and weeping I said, "Greetings, Lady." And she said to me, "Why so gloomy and sad, Hermas? You are patient and good-tempered and always cheerful." I said to her, "Because of an excellent woman who says I have sinned against her." **7** She said, "Far be this from a servant of God! But the thought did arise in you. Such a thought as this brings sin upon the servants of God. And it is an evil and shameful purpose when a righteous person entertains a wicked desire — most of all when Hermas the temperate, who abstains from all wicked desire and is full of simplicity and great innocence, does so." **8** "But God is not angry with you because of this, but to convert your household, which has sinned against the Lord, and against you their parents. Yet you are fond of your children and did not admonish your household. For this cause the Lord is wrathful with you. But he will heal all the past evils of your household. For on account of their sins and iniquities you have been consumed by the cares of this world. But the great mercy of the Lord has taken pity on you, and will establish you with your household, and strengthen you before his glory."

---

*EMET note: This is Vision 2, Chapter 1. Repetition of ch 2 material is deliberate — it appears Hermas received a second confirmation vision.*
